items.title: Integer division
items.goal: Print the exact average of `total` and `count`.
items.explanation: `total / count` is `int / int`, so Java divides first (giving `3`) and only then widens to `3.0`. Casting one operand *before* the division makes it a `double` division. Casting the whole `(total / count)` is too late: the fraction is already gone.

items.title: byte arithmetic
items.goal: Add 5 to the `byte` and print it.
items.explanation: Arithmetic on `byte`, `short` and `char` is done in `int`, so `b + 5` is an `int` and can't be assigned to a `byte` without a cast. Compound assignment (`+=`) includes an implicit cast back to `byte`. `(byte) b + 5` casts only `b`; the sum is still `int`.

items.title: Strings are immutable
items.goal: Print the word in upper case.
items.explanation: `String` is immutable: `toUpperCase()` returns a **new** string and leaves `s` alone. The result must be assigned back to `s` (or printed directly).

items.title: StringBuilder index
items.goal: Remove the trailing `s`, then print the text reversed.
items.explanation: Indexes run from `0` to `length() - 1`, so `deleteCharAt(sb.length())` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. `delete(start, end)` also throws when `start > end`.

items.title: == on strings
items.goal: Print `same` because both strings hold the same text.
items.explanation: `==` compares references. `new String("hi")` is a different object from the pooled literal, so `a == b` is `false`. `equals` compares the characters. `b.toString()` returns `b` itself, so it doesn't help, and `compareTo` returns `0` (not `1`) for equal strings.

items.title: Math.round returns long
items.goal: Round the price to the nearest whole number and print it.
items.explanation: `Math.round(double)` returns a `long`, which doesn't fit in an `int` without a cast. (`Math.round(float)` returns `int`.) Casting `price` itself truncates to `2`, and so does `floor`.

items.title: Text block opening
items.goal: Print the JSON text exactly as shown.
items.explanation: A text block's opening `"""` must be followed by a line break, so a one-line text block doesn't compile. A normal string literal works if the inner quotes are escaped as `\"`. Single quotes are for one `char`, and `\{` is not a valid escape in Java 21.

items.title: Missing break
items.goal: Print `weekend` for day 6.
items.explanation: Colon-style `case` labels fall through: without `break`, the `default` line runs next and overwrites `kind`. A block `{ }` doesn't stop fall-through, and one switch can't mix `:` and `->` labels.

items.title: yield in a block
items.goal: Print the price for size `M` (base 5 plus 2).
items.explanation: A block on the right of `->` in a switch **expression** must produce its value with `yield`. `return` would try to leave `main`, which isn't allowed from inside a switch expression, and `break value` was preview syntax that no longer exists.

items.title: Exhaustive switch
items.goal: Print `many` for code 3.
items.explanation: A switch **expression** must cover every possible value. For an `int` that means a `default` branch; listing more constants never makes it exhaustive.

items.title: Labeled break
items.goal: Stop at the first pair whose product is 6 and print it as `ij`.
items.explanation: A plain `break` only leaves the inner loop, so the outer loop keeps going and later finds `3 * 2` (32). `break outer;` leaves both loops. `continue outer;` skips to the next `i`, which still reaches 32, and a label must name a statement, not a variable.

items.title: Off by one
items.goal: Print the sum of the array.
items.explanation: Valid indexes are `0` to `length - 1`, so `i <= nums.length` reads one past the end and throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Arrays have a `length` **field**; `length()` is for `String`.

items.title: switch on null
items.goal: Print `unknown` when `cmd` is null.
items.explanation: A switch throws `NullPointerException` on a null selector unless it has a `case null` label; `default` does **not** match null. Java 21 lets you combine them as `case null, default ->`.

items.title: Shadowed field
items.goal: Print the count passed to the constructor.
items.explanation: Inside the constructor the parameter `count` shadows the field, so `count = count` assigns the parameter to itself and the field stays `0`. `this.count` names the field. `Counter.count` would need a static field.

items.title: Static context
items.goal: Count two hits from `main` and print the total.
items.explanation: `main` is static, so it has no `this` and can't touch an instance field. Making `hits` static fixes it; `static final` compiles the declaration but then `hits++` can't change a constant.

items.title: Overload resolution
items.goal: Make the call pick the `Integer` overload.
items.explanation: Java tries overloads in phases: widening first, then boxing/unboxing, then varargs. A `byte`, `short` or `int` widens to `long` in phase 1. A `Byte` unboxes and widens to `long` too; it is not an `Integer`. Only an `Integer` argument matches `kind(Integer)` exactly.

items.title: Records can't extend
items.goal: Print the square's area.
options: record Square(double side) extends Object implements Shape {
final record Square(double side) extends Shape {
items.explanation: A record implicitly extends `java.lang.Record`, so it can't have an `extends` clause at all, not even `extends Object`. It can implement interfaces. Only records have a header like `(double side)`.

items.title: Canonical constructor
items.goal: Validate the temperature and print the record.
items.explanation: A full canonical constructor must assign every field (`this.celsius = celsius;`), so this one doesn't compile. The **compact** form `Temp {` runs the check and assigns the fields automatically at the end. A `Temp()` constructor isn't canonical and would have to call `this(...)`.

items.title: var infers int
items.goal: Add up the prices and print the total.
items.explanation: `var` takes its type from the initializer: `0` makes `total` an `int`. `+=` silently casts each sum back to `int`, so the fractions vanish. `0L` makes it a `long` (same problem), `'0'` a `char`, and `var x = null;` doesn't compile because there's no type to infer.

items.title: Pass by value
items.goal: Add one to the array's element inside `grow`.
items.explanation: Java passes a **copy of the reference**. Reassigning `arr` points the local copy at a new array; the caller's array is untouched. Writing through the reference (`arr[0] = ...`) changes the shared object. `arr[0] = arr[0]++` stores the old value back, so it stays 41.

items.title: sealed permits
items.goal: Print the area of a 2 by 2 square.
options: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square {}
items.explanation: `Square` implements `Shape` but isn't in the `permits` list, which is a compile error. `permits` is only allowed on a `sealed` type, and every direct subtype must be listed (or the clause omitted when they're all in the same file).

items.title: Weaker access
items.goal: Print the dog's sound through an `Animal` reference.
items.explanation: An override can't reduce visibility: `public` stays `public`. The return type may be the same or a subtype (covariant), never a supertype like `Object`, and a static method can't hide an instance method.

items.title: Pattern variable scope
items.goal: Print the length of `o` when it's a non-empty string.
items.explanation: A pattern variable is only in scope where the match is **definitely true**. After `||` the left side may have failed, so `s` isn't usable there. With `&&` it is, and also inside the body. The non-short-circuit `|` evaluates both sides, so `s` isn't in scope either.

items.title: Default method conflict
items.goal: The duck should use `Walker`'s default `move`.
items.explanation: To call an inherited default method from a specific interface, use `Interface.super.method()`. `Walker.move()` looks like a static call and doesn't compile; `super.move()` means `Object`, which has no `move`; and `this.move()` calls itself until `StackOverflowError`.

items.title: Enum with fields
items.goal: Print the rank of `M`.
items.explanation: When an enum has fields, constructors or methods, the constant list must end with a semicolon. Constants are separated by commas and take constructor arguments in parentheses.

items.title: Fields don't override
items.goal: Print the child's name through a `Base` reference.
items.explanation: Fields are **hidden**, not overridden: `Base.name()` reads `Base`'s field no matter what `Child` declares. Only methods are polymorphic, so `Child` must override `name()`. Returning `name` from that override would still read the inherited `Base` field.

items.title: Inner class instance
items.goal: Create a `Greeter` and print its greeting.
items.explanation: An inner (non-static) class instance needs an enclosing `Main` object, and static `main` has none. `outer.new Inner()` supplies one. `this` doesn't exist in a static method.

items.title: Multi-catch types
items.goal: Catch the bad index and print its exception type.
items.explanation: The alternatives in a multi-catch may not be subclasses of each other: `IndexOutOfBoundsException` already is a `RuntimeException`, so the pair doesn't compile. A multi-catch has one variable name at the end.

items.title: Unreported checked exception
items.goal: Catch the failure from `load` and print its message.
items.explanation: `load` declares `IOException`, a checked exception, so the caller must catch `IOException` (or a supertype) or declare it. Catching only the subclass `FileNotFoundException` doesn't cover what the signature allows. `IOException | Exception` is illegal because one is a subclass of the other.

items.title: Effectively final resource
items.goal: Use resource `b` and close it.
items.explanation: Since Java 9 a try-with-resources header may name an existing variable, but only if it's final or effectively final, and `r` is reassigned. Declaring a new resource variable initialized from `r` works. A resource declaration always needs an initializer.

items.title: Overriding and throws
items.goal: Load through the interface and print the data.
options: public String load() throws IOException, Exception {
items.explanation: An overriding method may throw fewer or narrower checked exceptions, never broader ones: `Exception` and `Throwable` are wider than `IOException`. Throwing nothing is always allowed. Dropping `public` is a weaker access level, which is also illegal.

items.title: Declaring throws
items.goal: Report the failure as `Exception: negative: -5`.
options: static void validate(int n) throws RuntimeException {
static void validate(int n) throws Exception {
static void validate(int n) catch Exception {
static void validate(int n) throw Exception {
items.explanation: Throwing a checked `Exception` requires the method to declare it with `throws` (note the **s**). Declaring only `RuntimeException` doesn't cover a checked exception.

items.title: Closing order
items.goal: Close `A` before `B`.
options: try (R a = new R("A"); R b = new R("B");) {
try (R b = new R("B"); R a = new R("A")) {
try (R b = new R("A"); R a = new R("B")) {
try (R a = new R("A"), R b = new R("B")) {
items.explanation: Resources are closed in **reverse** order of declaration, so the last one opened closes first. To close `A` first, declare it last. Resources are separated by semicolons; a trailing semicolon is allowed but changes nothing.

items.title: Immutable list
items.goal: Add `Cy`, sort and print the names.
items.explanation: `List.of` and `List.copyOf` return unmodifiable lists, so `add` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. `Arrays.asList` is fixed-size: `set` works but `add` throws. Copy into an `ArrayList` to get a growable list.

items.title: Removing while iterating
items.goal: Remove the even numbers and print the rest.
items.explanation: Changing an `ArrayList` during a for-each loop makes the iterator throw `ConcurrentModificationException`. `removeIf` removes safely. With `int n`, `remove(n)` would also pick the remove-by-**index** overload.

items.title: remove(int) vs remove(Object)
items.goal: Remove the value 10 and print the list.
items.explanation: `List<Integer>` has `remove(int index)` and `remove(Object o)`. An `int` argument picks the index version (no boxing needed), so `remove(10)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. Pass an `Integer` to remove by value.

items.title: Reversed comparator
items.goal: Sort the words longest first.
items.explanation: `reversed()` is a method, so it needs parentheses. `reverseOrder()` reverses the natural (alphabetical) order, not the length order.

items.title: Comparing arrays
items.goal: Print whether the arrays hold the same numbers.
items.explanation: Arrays don't override `equals`, so `a.equals(b)` is `==`: two different arrays are never equal. `Arrays.equals` compares the elements. `compare` returns `0` and `mismatch` returns `-1` for equal arrays.

items.title: Counting with a map
items.goal: Count each letter of `banana`.
items.explanation: `get` returns `null` for a missing key and unboxing `null + 1` throws `NullPointerException`. `merge(key, 1, Integer::sum)` stores `1` the first time and adds afterwards. `compute` passes `null` for a missing key too.

items.title: Reusing a stream
items.goal: Print the count and the joined words.
items.explanation: A stream can be consumed only once: after `count()` any further operation on `s` throws `IllegalStateException`. Create a fresh stream from the list. Lists have no `collect` method.

items.title: Effectively final capture
items.goal: Print the sum of the list.
items.explanation: A lambda may only use local variables that are final or effectively final, so it can't modify `count`. Compute the value with a stream and assign it outside the lambda. `count()` counts elements (3), it doesn't add them.

items.title: Duplicate keys in toMap
items.goal: Keep the first word for each starting letter.
items.explanation: Two-argument `toMap` throws `IllegalStateException` on a duplicate key (`a`). The third argument is a merge function: `(a, b) -> a` keeps the existing value. `groupingBy` would build `Map<Character, List<String>>`, which doesn't match the declared type.

items.title: Empty Optional
items.goal: Print the first even number, or -1 if there is none.
items.explanation: `findFirst()` returns an empty `Optional` here, and `get()` / `orElseThrow()` on an empty Optional throw `NoSuchElementException`. `orElse(null)` returns `null`, which fails when unboxed to `int`.

items.title: average needs a primitive stream
items.goal: Print the average score.
items.explanation: `Stream<Integer>` has no `average()`; only `IntStream`, `LongStream` and `DoubleStream` do. `average()` returns an `OptionalDouble`, so you still need `orElse` to get a `double`.

items.title: Lazy streams
items.goal: Record every element the stream visits.
items.explanation: Intermediate operations are lazy: nothing runs until a terminal operation such as `toList()`. `sorted()` is intermediate too. Trap: since Java 9, `count()` may skip the pipeline when the size is known, so `peek` never runs.

items.title: counting() is Long
items.goal: Count words by length with `Collectors.counting()`.
items.explanation: `Collectors.counting()` produces a `Long`, so the map is `Map<Integer, Long>`. The key type comes from the classifier `String::length`, an `Integer`.

items.title: Choosing a functional interface
items.goal: Greet with a lambda that takes and returns a `String`.
items.explanation: `Supplier.get()` takes no argument. A function from `String` to `String` is `UnaryOperator<String>` (a `Function<String, String>`) with method `apply`. `Consumer` returns nothing, `Predicate` returns `boolean`, and `BiFunction` takes three type arguments.

items.title: Future.get throws
items.goal: Print the task's result.
options: public static void main(String[] args) throws RuntimeException {
public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
public static void main(String[] args) throws ExecutionException {
public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
items.explanation: `Future.get()` declares two checked exceptions, `InterruptedException` and `ExecutionException`, so both must be handled or declared. `throws Exception` covers both. (Since Java 19 `ExecutorService` is `AutoCloseable`; `close()` waits for submitted tasks.)

items.title: Lock before unlock
items.goal: Increment the counter twice under the lock.
items.explanation: The idiom is `lock.lock(); try { ... } finally { lock.unlock(); }`. Calling `unlock()` on a lock the thread doesn't hold throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`, and a `synchronized` block uses the object's monitor, not the `ReentrantLock`.

items.title: notifyAll needs the monitor
items.goal: Notify waiting threads, then print `notified`.
items.explanation: `wait`, `notify` and `notifyAll` may only be called while holding **that object's** monitor, otherwise they throw `IllegalMonitorStateException`. Locking a different object doesn't count, and `this` doesn't exist in static `main`.

items.title: Starting a virtual thread
items.goal: Run the task on a virtual thread, wait for it, then print `isVirtual()`.
options: Thread t = new Thread(() -> System.out.println("hi"), true);
items.explanation: `Thread.Builder` has `start(task)` (create and start) and `unstarted(task)` (create only); there is no `run`. Joining a thread that was never started returns at once, so the task never prints. `join()` returns `void`.

items.title: AtomicInteger isn't an int
items.goal: Count 1000 hits from a thread pool.
items.explanation: `AtomicInteger` is an object, so `++` and `+=` don't compile on it. `incrementAndGet()` adds atomically. `get() + 1` only computes a value and never stores it. Closing the pool waits for all tasks, so the count is exact.

items.title: Adding while iterating
items.goal: Append an exclaimed copy of each element.
items.explanation: `CopyOnWriteArrayList` iterates over a snapshot, so adding during the loop is safe and the loop only sees the original two elements. A synchronized wrapper is still fail-fast and throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.

items.title: resolve with an absolute path
items.goal: Build the path of today's log inside the app folder.
items.explanation: `resolve` with an **absolute** argument just returns the argument. Pass a relative path to append it. `resolveSibling` resolves against the parent (`/data`), and `relativize` needs two paths of the same kind (both absolute or both relative).

items.title: relativize direction
items.goal: Print how to get from the docs folder to the picture.
items.explanation: `a.relativize(b)` gives the path that leads **from a to b**, so the starting folder is the receiver. `to.relativize(from)` walks the other way (`../../docs`).

items.title: readLine loop
items.goal: Print each line of the file.
items.explanation: The line read must be stored before it's tested: `(line = r.readLine()) != null`. Without the assignment `line` is never initialized, which is a compile error. The parentheses matter: `!=` binds tighter than `=`.

items.title: Serializable marker
items.goal: Serialize the user, read it back and print its fields.
items.explanation: `writeObject` throws `NotSerializableException` unless the class implements `Serializable`. When the object is read back its constructor and field initializers don't run, so the `transient` field gets its default value `0`, not `7`.

items.title: readAllLines returns a List
items.goal: Count the lines longer than one character.
items.explanation: `Files.readAllLines` returns a `List<String>`, which has no `filter`. `Files.lines` returns a lazy `Stream<String>`. `Files.list` streams the entries of a **directory** as `Path`s.

items.title: Creating nested folders
items.goal: Create the report folder and confirm it exists.
items.explanation: `createDirectory` creates one level and throws `NoSuchFileException` when the parent is missing. `createDirectories` creates every missing parent. `File.mkdir()` doesn't throw; it just returns `false`.

items.title: LocalDate is immutable
items.goal: Move the due date one month later.
items.explanation: `LocalDate` is immutable: `plusMonths` returns a new date that must be assigned. Adding a month to January 31 clamps to the last valid day, February 29 in a leap year.

items.title: Months start at 1
items.goal: Print January 15, 2024.
items.explanation: In `java.time`, months run from 1 to 12, so month `0` throws `DateTimeException`. `Month.JANUARY` (or `1`) is right. `Month.of(0)` fails the same way.

items.title: MM vs mm
items.goal: Format the date as day/month/year.
items.explanation: Pattern letters are case-sensitive: `MM` is month, `mm` is **minute** (here `05`). `DD` is day-of-year, single letters drop the leading zero, and `MMM` gives the short month name.

items.title: Duration vs Period
items.goal: Print the gap between the dates in months and days.
items.explanation: `Duration` measures time-based amounts (seconds, nanos) and needs times, so `Duration.between` on two `LocalDate`s throws `UnsupportedTemporalTypeException`. `Period` measures date-based amounts (years, months, days). A `Duration` of days prints in hours (`PT1776H`).

items.title: NumberFormat locale
items.goal: Format the number with German grouping (the default locale is en_US).
items.explanation: Without an argument `NumberFormat.getInstance()` uses the default locale (`1,234.5` for en_US). Pass the locale. `getIntegerInstance` rounds to a whole number (half-even: `1.234`) and `getCurrencyInstance` adds the currency.

items.title: Parsing a custom format
items.goal: Parse the date text and print its weekday.
items.explanation: `LocalDate.parse(text)` expects ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` and throws `DateTimeParseException` otherwise. Pass a formatter with the matching pattern. With `mm` the `03` is read as minutes, so no month is parsed and it still fails.

items.title: Reading another module
items.goal: Run `com.shop.app`, which calls `Price.tag()`.
items.explanation: A module reads another with `requires <module>`. `exports` and `opens` name packages of the module **itself**, and `requires` takes a module name, not a class.

items.title: exports takes a package
items.goal: Let `com.shop.app` (which requires `com.shop.api`) call `Price.tag()`.
items.explanation: `exports` names a **package**, never a class. `opens` only allows deep reflection at run time; code in other modules still can't compile against the package. A module can't require itself.
items.context: Module `com.shop.app` requires `com.shop.api` and calls `Price.tag()` from its `Main`.

items.title: uses vs provides
items.goal: Load every `Payment` service and print its name.
items.explanation: The consumer of a service declares `uses <interface>`; the provider declares `provides <interface> with <class>`. Without `uses`, `ServiceLoader.load` throws `ServiceConfigurationError`, even if the provider module is readable.
items.context: `com.pay.api` exports interface `Payment`; `com.pay.card` provides it with class `Card`.

items.title: Implied readability
items.goal: Let `com.app`, which requires only `com.lib.util`, use the `Core` it gets back.
items.explanation: `requires transitive` passes readability on: every module that reads `com.lib.util` also reads `com.lib.core`. Use it when your exported API exposes another module's types. `requires static` is a compile-time-only dependency and isn't passed on.
items.context: `com.lib.core` exports `Core`. `com.app` requires only `com.lib.util`, and its `Main` does `Core c = Util.make();`.

items.title: Deep reflection needs opens
items.goal: Let `com.app` read the private field by reflection.
items.explanation: `exports` gives access to **public** members only; `setAccessible(true)` on a private field throws `InaccessibleObjectException` unless the package is **opened** (`opens`, or an `open module`).
